relevance_note: Review of treatments in SSADH deficiency that lists individual previously published patients with sex, age and VGB response (Table 1: 'Outcomes of VGB intervention in SSADH Deficiency') and per-patient CSF data (Table 2), plus individual detail on a taurine-treated patient ('The patient, a 2-year old male'); no ALDH5A1 variant is printed for anyone.
method_note: Built with a short Python script in the scratch directory; Table 1 and Table 2 rows were transcribed by hand into the script and checked against the paper, and every span was checked verbatim by script. Table 1 (no label column) rows are 'Table 1 row k'; its 'Age (yrs)' column (header 'Age (yrs)', unit years) is recorded as age at last evaluation/time of report, though it may be age at VGB treatment; its Reference column is copied into source_reference_in_review. Table 1 'Clinical Improvement' entries (ataxia, hypotonia, EEG (swd), myoclonus, hyperactivity, agitation behavior) are recorded as observed features because improvement of a sign presupposes the sign; vague entries ('none', 'IQ', 'cognition, behavior (low dose)', 'communication') were not turned into features; hyperactivity and agitation behavior were not mapped to the checklist items 'attention problems or ADHD' or 'aggression or disruptive behavior'. Table 2 (bare patient numbers 1-4) rows are 'Table 2 #n', reprinted from Gibson et al 1995; their treatment comes from the text statement about the same four patients; the CSF GHB/GABA values were not turned into 'elevated' features because the paper states no per-patient elevation, only control ranges. Table 2 patients may overlap with Table 1 patients or with each other's source reports; not merged. The Saronwala and colleagues (2008) patient's age '2-year old' is the age at the start of taurine treatment, recorded as age at last evaluation; 'T2 signal MRI abnormality' is not stated as a hyperintensity, so the T2 checklist item is left not reported. 'unnamed person 1' is the one open-label taurine trial patient with a serious adverse event (hypersomnia), recorded as observed hypersomnia and checklist 'sleep disturbances' observed although it is a treatment adverse event. The other 15 trial patients, the 23 VGB MRI patients ('8 of 23'), Jakobs' three patients, Matern et al 1996's worsening seizure control (text not attributed to a specific person) and GABA-T deficiency patients get no rows (group-level only or out of scope). cohort_size_as_stated is the taurine trial's 16. No contradictions found; Table 1's notes are printed twice.
